perspective:
From Jose Castillo’s perspective:

- He works with Patricia Ndiaye at a community bank, where he sometimes helps with maintenance and repairs. They have a friendly, professional relationship.
- He noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn than usual recently and remembered her as normally being vibrant.
- He asked if she was okay. She said it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked him for asking.
- He offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk. She said she appreciated it and that it meant a lot.
- During a lunch break, he overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He brought up financial planning and offered to discuss budgeting strategies with her. She said it could be helpful and admitted she had been overwhelmed with bills lately.
- He offered to go over budgeting tips together whenever she felt up to it. She thanked him and said she’d take him up on it soon.
- Later, he worried he might have overstepped, so he clarified that he wanted to help, not pry. She said she didn’t think he was prying and was grateful for the offer.
- He told her he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend. She said she really appreciated it and was glad to have someone to turn to.
- Later, he asked how she was doing and about her weekend plans. She said she was fine and planned a quiet weekend at home.
- He continued to check in with her at work and offered support, even just for something small like grabbing coffee. She said she was busy but handling it, thanked him for checking in, and said it was great to have his support.
- He sensed that Patricia appreciated his concern but preferred to handle her personal matters privately. He doesn’t know the exact details of her personal situation or the full extent of her financial struggles.
